title: af/storage-prune@2
description: `af storage prune --json` (ADR-0144): what one sweep removed, or without --apply would remove. A sweep plans once over one inventory snapshot and the applied sweep runs that plan entry by entry, never choosing again (ADR-0152 clause 13): first the deletions interruptions left (rule `recovery`), then collection (rule `collection`, and `keep_surveys` for the Surveys of a Project beyond `[storage] keep_surveys`), then the budget, least recently used first (rule `budget`), until the total fits `max_bytes` or nothing else may be removed (`stop`). Each removal says what it frees and af's total after it: as planned in a preview, as freed by the applied sweep. Gate cleanups of finished Tasks are those the sweep tried; registry entries whose path holds no Store any more are dropped; a failed removal is listed and tried again by the next sweep. Version 2 adds the removal kind `survey` (ADR-0152 clause 13): a Survey's record in its Project Store's CAS, its `path` the CAS object, taken behind a `SurveyCollected@1` tombstone. A Survey whose record's bytes were no Survey is removed with `unreadable`, the reason its tombstone carries; a Survey whose job found what the plan did not (the lock lost, its record replaced) keeps its place in the applied sweep's removals with nothing freed and `deviation`. What the plan leaves is listed under `left`, by the preview and the applied sweep alike, with its reason: `held` (its Project Store's `project.lock` cannot be taken now), `foreign` (a file at a collected Survey's CAS name after its record was moved, or anything under `cas/removing` that is no collected Survey's record; never deleted, and counted in its Project Store's bytes, never a Survey's), `oversize` (a record over 1 MiB) or `unreadable_name` (a name under `cas/removing` that is not UTF-8). A Survey whose record cannot be reached without a link or read is a failure, and keeps its record and its place in the log.

total_after.description: af's total after this removal: as planned in a preview, after what the applied sweep freed.

unreadable.description: A `survey` removal only: why its record's bytes were no Survey, as its `SurveyCollected@1` tombstone says.

deviation.description: The applied sweep, a `survey` removal only: what its job found that the plan did not, so it freed nothing (`bytes` 0); the next sweep plans again.

left.description: What the plan leaves where it is (ADR-0152 clause 13), by the preview and the applied sweep alike. The next pass plans again.

path.description: The path as it is when it is UTF-8; otherwise in the canonical percent-encoded spelling of `review_core::encode_path`, with `path_encoded`.
